https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/respiratory-syncytial-virus-rsv-guidance-data-and-analysis
UKHSA RSV guidance, data and analysis collection
RSV symptoms, diagnosis, treatment, management, surveillance and epidemiology
The collection brings together official advice on RSV symptoms, diagnosis, treatment, management and epidemiology.
It identifies RSV as a common winter respiratory virus and a major cause of bronchiolitis in children under 2 years.
rsv_vaccination_collection
https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/respiratory-syncytial-virus-rsv-vaccination-programme
UKHSA RSV vaccination programme collection
national RSV vaccination programmes for older adults, care-home residents and pregnant women
The collection brings together national RSV vaccination programme publications.
It covers the routine older-adult programme and the programme for pregnant women to protect infants.
rsv_hcp_landing
https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/respiratory-syncytial-virus-rsv-programme-information-for-healthcare-professionals
UKHSA RSV programme healthcare-professional publication
delivery of maternal and older-adult RSV vaccination programmes
The publication provides healthcare-professional guidance for maternal and older-adult RSV vaccination.
It states that pregnant women should be offered vaccination from week 28 of pregnancy.
rsv_older_adults_detail
https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/respiratory-syncytial-virus-rsv-programme-information-for-healthcare-professionals/rsv-vaccination-of-older-adults-information-for-healthcare-practioners
UKHSA RSV older-adult practitioner guidance
eligibility, catch-up, care-home delivery and authorisation for older-adult RSV vaccination
The guidance specifies routine and catch-up eligibility for older-adult RSV vaccination.
From April 2026 it includes adults aged 75 years and older who have not received a dose.

https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/respiratory-syncytial-virus-rsv-programme-information-for-healthcare-professionals/rsv-vaccination-of-pregnant-women-for-infant-protection-information-for-healthcare-practitioners
UKHSA maternal RSV practitioner guidance
maternal RSV vaccination to protect infants
The guidance is specifically for the maternal RSV programme that protects infants.
It states that vaccination should be offered from 28 weeks of pregnancy.
rsv_green_book
https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/respiratory-syncytial-virus-the-green-book
UKHSA RSV Green Book chapter
national RSV immunisation policy, safety, efficacy and selective immunisation
The chapter provides RSV immunisation information for public-health professionals.
It includes current evidence on vaccine safety and effectiveness.

https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/rsv-vaccination-for-older-adults-expansion-of-eligibility/expansion-of-rsv-vaccine-eligibility-to-those-aged-80-years-and-older-and-residents-in-care-homes-for-older-adults-letter
NHS RSV older-adult eligibility expansion letter
April 2026 expansion of older-adult RSV vaccine eligibility
The letter announces expansion to adults aged 80 years and older and all residents of older-adult care homes.
The eligibility change took effect on 1 April 2026.

https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/rsv-vaccination-for-older-adults-expansion-of-eligibility/annexe-a-detailed-information-guidance-and-resources-for-healthcare-professionals
UKHSA RSV 80-plus expansion implementation annex
implementation, supply, co-administration and coverage monitoring for expanded RSV eligibility
The annex provides implementation information for the April 2026 RSV expansion.
It explains vaccine supply through ImmForm and ordering preparation.

https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/rsv-vaccination-expansion-of-eligibility-to-older-adults-in-certain-clinical-risk-groups/expansion-of-eligibility-to-adults-aged-65-to-74-years-in-certain-clinical-at-risk-groups-letter
UKHSA RSV clinical-risk eligibility expansion letter
September 2026 RSV eligibility for adults aged 65 to 74 in specified clinical-risk groups
The letter announces further RSV programme expansion from 1 September 2026.
It includes adults aged 65 to 74 years in specified clinical-risk groups.
